title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: UGC Funding and Institutional Autonomy
body_text:
The details of total funds released by the Ministry of Education and utilised by the University Grants Commission (UGC) during 2021-22 to 2025-26, are as under:
(Rs. in Crore)
Year 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 Fund released 13839.43 16859.87 19054.74 19770.47 20527.43 Expenditure 13606.52 16080.55 18676.31 19742.07 20507.48
Out of the total funds released to UGC during the period 2021-22 to 2025-26, funds amounting to Rs. 73,148.65 crore and Rs. 2,743.04 Crore have been released by UGC to the Central Universities and Institutions Deemed to be Universities respectively.
The Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS), was launched in 2013 with the objective of providing funding to eligible State Higher Educational Institutions. The aim of this scheme is to achieve mass access to higher education with high quality standards. Funding is provided to the State Universities and Colleges by the Department of Higher Education, Government of India under RUSA.
The Government launched the third phase of RUSA in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26. Under the Scheme, support is provided to States/UTs for strengthening infrastructure, including construction of hostels, academic and administrative buildings, laboratories and other facilities required for improving access and quality in higher education.
The year-wise details of Central Share released to the States/UTs under PM-USHA/RUSA during the last five financial years and current financial year are as given below:
(Rs.in Crore)
Year 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 2026-27 (As on 06.08.2026) Central Share Released 249.13 359.50 181.06 350.83 864.25 507.00
After implementation of the RUSA, UGC does not provide any development grants to State Universities per se. After the 12th Plan period, UGC has released funds to State Universities, including private universities, only for settlement on reimbursement basis under the UGC Schemes sanctioned earlier. Towards this expenditure, total funds amounting to Rs. 931.44 crore have been released by UGC during the period 2021-22 to 2025-26. Further, an amount of Rs.1818.46 crore was released to Punjab University, an Inter-State Body Corporate, as fixed salary grant during the same period.
The UGC (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and other Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education) Regulations, 2018, notified on 18th July 2018, inter alia provide for the minimum qualification for appointment and other service conditions of University and College teachers, Librarians, and Directors of Physical Education and Sports as a measure for the maintenance of standards in higher education.
The National Education Policy (NEP) envisages a ‘light but tight’ regulatory framework to ensure integrity, transparency, and resource efficiency of the educational system through audit and public disclosure while encouraging innovation and out-of-the-box ideas through autonomy, good governance, and empowerment. Accordingly, the Ministry has introduced the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 in Lok Sabha on December 15, 2025. This Bill has been referred to a Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
*****
RRTN

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Education gave year-wise data (2021-22 to 2025-26) on UGC fund releases and expenditure, funds channelled to Central Universities and Deemed Universities, and Central Share released to States/UTs under RUSA/PM-USHA. It also noted that UGC no longer gives development grants to State Universities post-RUSA implementation, referenced the UGC 2018 teacher-qualification Regulations, and confirmed that the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025, introduced in Lok Sabha on 15 December 2025, has been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
enrichment.context:
The Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), launched in 2013, was India's first major Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at channelling central funds to state higher education institutions (which fall outside UGC's direct funding ambit for development grants) to improve access, equity, and quality. Its third phase, rebranded Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) in June 2023, continues this mandate through 2025-26, focusing on infrastructure like hostels, labs, and academic buildings, reflecting NEP 2020's Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) targets for higher education (to reach 50% by 2035). Since RUSA's rollout, UGC's role for state universities has been reduced mainly to settling legacy dues from schemes sanctioned before the 12th Plan, marking a functional bifurcation between UGC (for central/deemed universities) and state governments/RUSA-PM-USHA (for state universities).

The mention of the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025, is significant: this legislation is understood to be part of the broader NEP 2020 vision of a 'light but tight' regulatory architecture, potentially restructuring or replacing the UGC itself (echoing the earlier, lapsed Higher Education Commission of India Bill proposals) to create a single regulator for higher education while granting institutions greater academic and administrative autonomy. Its referral to a Joint Committee of Parliament indicates continuing legislative scrutiny and stakeholder consultation before any structural overhaul of higher education regulation in India. The UGC (Minimum Qualifications) Regulations, 2018, remain the operative framework governing teacher recruitment standards, underscoring the tension NEP seeks to resolve between regulatory oversight and institutional autonomy.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding RUSA/PM-USHA:
1. RUSA was launched in 2013 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for funding State Higher Educational Institutions.
2. PM-USHA is the third phase of RUSA, launched in June 2023.
3. Central Share under PM-USHA is released by the University Grants Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: RUSA (2013) and its third phase PM-USHA (June 2023) are correctly described. However, Central Share under PM-USHA/RUSA is released by the Department of Higher Education, not by UGC; UGC funds Central Universities and Deemed Universities separately. Hence only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

prelims_questions.question: The UGC (Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers...) Regulations were notified in which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, these Regulations were notified on 18th July 2018, prescribing minimum qualifications and service conditions for university/college teachers and staff.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the evolution of Centre-State funding architecture in higher education in India, with reference to RUSA/PM-USHA and the changing role of the UGC. How does this reflect the federal division of responsibilities envisaged under the National Education Policy 2020?

The National Education Policy 2020 envisages a 'light but tight' regulatory framework for higher education. Critically examine how the proposed Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 seeks to operationalise this vision, and discuss the implications for institutional autonomy versus regulatory oversight.
